CHIEF COMPLAINT
Rash with residual symptoms

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient reports rash is doing much better but has a small bit leftover. She initially took doxycycline twice daily and noticed significant improvement. Last week she reduced to once daily on pharmacist's recommendation, but reports improvement has plateaued and the rash is not continuing to get better. She denies currently breastfeeding. She started doxycycline after stopping breastfeeding. She had not been using elidel due to concerns after reading about it. Patient is using sulfacetamide wash twice daily without excessive dryness. She applies metro cream after face washing. She is not using any other lotions, cetaphil cleanser, or neutrogena wipes. Physical examination reveals Fitzpatrick skin type IV-V. Bilateral medial cheeks show a few faint erythematous papules with mild redness around and underneath nostrils. Patient reports sun sensitivity and takes precautions with hat and sun protection.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Patient denies excessive facial dryness from current regimen. Reports sun sensitivity with current medications.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Perioral dermatitis, rosacea, including ocular rosacea.

MEDICATIONS
Doxycycline (currently once daily, to be increased to twice daily)
Sulfacetamide wash (twice daily)
Metro cream (after face wash)

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Not discussed.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Fitzpatrick skin type IV-V. Bilateral medial cheeks with a few faint erythematous papules. Mild erythema around and underneath nostrils.

RESULTS
Not discussed.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Perioral dermatitis, rosacea, including ocular rosacea. Continue sulfacetamide wash once daily. Continue metro cream. Increase doxycycline to twice daily until rash resolves, then once daily for one week before stopping. Initiate tacrolimus ointment (calcineurin inhibitor, not a steroid) applied to rash area twice daily until resolved. Patient counseled that tacrolimus may cause transient tingly or needle-like sensation or redness for a few seconds after application. Once rash resolves, discontinue tacrolimus but continue doxycycline for one week. Continue wash and metro cream indefinitely. Hold off on old products until follow-up visit. If minor flare occurs, may try tacrolimus alone for a couple days. If worsening, patient to contact provider. Cancel elidel cream and clindamycin from medication list. Recommend moisturizer such as vanicream or petroleum jelly as needed. Provided samples of moisturizer. Patient counseled to avoid anti-aging products and plant-based products; reach out before trying new products. Gently wash eyelids once daily with gentle cleanser such as vanicream; use Bruder mask as needed. Follow-up appointment in approximately four weeks. Patient to contact if worsening or with questions.
